title: AI & Market Intelligence Briefing
headline: This week’s AI news paired the rapid expansion of agentic products and infrastructure with extraordinary funding ambitions and sharper public-sector and regulatory scrutiny.

items.text: Anthropic introduced Claude Code mods: TypeScript functions packaged in plugins that can change prompts, tool handling and interface behavior. Mods run with Claude Code’s machine access and are not sandboxed, making trusted-source controls important.

Anthropic’s IPO prospectus disclosed the cost of frontier-AI scale: nearly $4.6 billion in 2025 revenue alongside a $42 billion reported net loss, substantially affected by an accounting charge, and $518 billion in planned cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations.
ChatGPT added virtual try-on for clothing and accessories plus saved Favorites, extending its shopping features across mobile and web.

Google launched a Project Suncatcher prototype satellite carrying four Tensor Processing Units to test AI chips in space; the research is an early step toward assessing orbital data-center concepts, not a commercial space data center.

AMD said it would acquire Fei-Fei Li’s World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at $8.2 billion, adding spatial-intelligence research aimed at physical AI; the transaction is expected to close by year-end.
Nvidia raised its share-repurchase authorization by a record $150 billion as investors weigh the sustainability of the AI infrastructure boom and intensifying chip competition.
AI-agent startup Instinct confirmed a $1 billion Series C valuing it at $10 billion, roughly a month after a prior round valued it at $2.5 billion.
TechCrunch reported that inference provider Modal Labs was nearing a $750 million round at a $15.75 billion valuation, citing a source familiar with the deal; the company declined to comment.
Reuters, citing Bloomberg, reported that OpenAI was seeking at least $30 billion in new funding at an approximately $1.4 trillion valuation; discussions were early-stage and terms could change.
Anthropic made Claude for Government generally available to federal and state agencies in a FedRAMP High-authorized environment, with Claude Code CLI and Claude for Microsoft 365 in early access.

President Trump said AI-company leaders signed a voluntary accord for internal and external reviews after a White House meeting; AP reported that the accord’s text was not yet public and details remained under discussion.

Google challenged EU orders requiring it to open certain services to AI rivals and search competitors, arguing the measures threaten privacy and security; the European Commission said it would defend the orders.
